title: Three records fall as TCS Sydney Marathon runs the fastest marathon ever on Australian soil
claims: Addisu Gobena won the 2026 men's race in 2:04:42, taking 1 minute 24 seconds off the previous race record of 2:06:06 set by Hailemaryam Kiros in 2025.
Chimdessa Debele Gudeta finished second in 2:04:46 and Tebello Ramakongoana third in 2:04:57; Alphonce Simbu finished fourth in 2:04:57.
The race report states that three men broke 2:05:00 and that the men's podium was faster than any previously seen on Australian soil.
The race report says five men finished under 2:05 on Australian soil and that all three podium men finished inside the previous race record, alongside four others.
Peres Jepchirchir won the women's race in 2:18:31, 3 minutes 40 seconds ahead of Irine Cheptai in 2:22:11, with Shure Demise Ware third in 2:22:33.
Jepchirchir finished nine seconds outside Sifan Hassan's 2025 race record of 2:18:22.
Daniel Romanchuk won the men's wheelchair race in 1:26:50, lowering the race and Australian all-comers record of 1:27:15 set by Marcel Hug in 2025.
Manuela Schär won the women's wheelchair race in 1:42:04, taking 2 minutes 48 seconds off Susannah Scaroni's course record of 1:44:52.
Andy Buchanan won the Australian men's championship in 2:10:14, with Tim Vincent second in 2:13:54 and Liam Boudin third in 2:14:58.
Ellie Pashley won the Australian women's championship in 2:28:28, with Milly Clark second in 2:29:47 and Caitlin Scott third in 2:31:11.
The race report describes the 2026 event as the fastest race in Australian history and says three of the four race records were broken.
